scoutClaimReconciliation.claim: MIT LICENSE at the tag (Copyright 2015-present Drifty Co.)
scoutClaimReconciliation.finding: materially wrong on both counts. The root LICENSE file at commit a7b2fc6afcd064947f3623774f4fd7db83c53c9c is the full Apache License 2.0 text (11,341 bytes), whose appendix carries the notice "Copyright 2015 Drifty Co." — not "2015-present", and not an MIT grant. package.json at the same revision independently declares "license": "Apache-2.0". The two agree with each other and disagree with the scout.
scoutClaimReconciliation.howDetected: The LICENSE blob is 11,341 bytes. An MIT file is roughly one kilobyte; 11 KB is Apache-2.0 length. The repository metadata response also reported spdx_id NOASSERTION rather than MIT. Both signals were followed to the file text rather than rounded off.
scoutClaimReconciliation.consequence: The packet's first admission gate — MIT LICENSE file content at the exact pinned revision — fails. Per the packet, this is recorded and returned as blocked, not worked around.

artifacts.textForm: The unmodified Apache License 2.0 boilerplate: the title block, the nine numbered sections of terms and conditions, END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS, and the "How to apply" appendix with the copyright field filled in as "Copyright 2015 Drifty Co." followed by the standard three-paragraph Apache notice. No MIT text appears anywhere in the file.

obligations: Retain the copyright, patent, trademark, and attribution notices from the source (section 4(c)).
Include a copy of the licence with any distribution of the work or derivative works (section 4(a)).
State significant changes made to the files in any modified version (section 4(b)).

Section 3 carries an express patent grant with a patent-litigation termination clause; MIT has no analogue. This is the substantive difference from the corpus's stated MIT requirement, not a formatting difference.
apacheTwoObligationsIfEverAdmitted.trademarkNote: Section 6 grants no trademark rights. "Ionic" and the Ionic marks belong to Drifty Co. / Ionic; the application's branding and artwork are carried only as part of the acquired upstream source.
